key_insight: A GaOx hole transport layer can be made conductive in 1.0 eV CuInSe2 bottom cells via ion-exchange during co-evaporation, enabling strong passivation and high voltage without extra Cu, Na, or heavy-alkali additives.
engineering_relevance: This shows a practical back-contact/passivation strategy for high-efficiency chalcopyrite tandem bottom cells, helping achieve >16% active-area efficiency and a record 552 mV VOC in CuInSe2.
method: Formed GaOx during co-evaporation of the low-bandgap absorber using ion exchange.
Tested whether Cu addition, Na, and oxygen flow during oxide sputtering affect GaOx conductivity.
Analyzed the structural state of the GaOx layer and its impact on device passivation and performance.
evidence_signal: The optimized devices reached above 16% active-area efficiency with a record-certified open-circuit voltage of 552 mV, indicating effective hole transport and suppressed recombination.
watch_item: The conductive behavior appears tied to a partly crystalline GaOx formed under specific process conditions, so transferability to other back-contact stacks or deposition windows may need re-optimization.
paper_title: What enables GaOx as hole transport layer for a 16 percent 1.0 eV CuInSe2 Bottom Cells with VOC above 550 mV?
